recent_posts.title: Apple to let users swap third-party AI models in iOS 27 via Extensions
recent_posts.summary: Apple plans to let users choose third-party AI models to power Apple Intelligence features in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27. Called 'Extensions,' the capability will be accessible via the Settings app and open to AI providers who add compatibility through their App Store apps. Apple has internally tested integrations with Google and Anthropic. The move comes as Apple tries to catch up with Google and Microsoft on AI, with more details expected at WWDC in June.

recent_posts.title: How Panther Lake put Intel back in contention
recent_posts.summary: Intel's Panther Lake chips, built on the new 18A process node, mark the company's first genuinely competitive CPU lineup since 2017. After nearly a decade of manufacturing missteps — starting with the troubled 10nm transition — Intel has regained ground against Apple Silicon and AMD Ryzen in both laptop and desktop segments. Independent reviews confirm 20+ hours of battery life on reference designs, and AMD has responded with defensive benchmarks, signaling real competitive pressure. The 18A fab in Arizona also positions Intel as a credible US-based alternative to TSMC for leading-edge chip manufacturing. Intel's stock has crossed $100 for the first time, though analysts caution the rally may be premature given the foundry business remains unprofitable.

recent_posts.title: Securex South Africa 2026 – five expos under one roof
recent_posts.summary: Securex South Africa 2026 is a three-day event (2–4 June) at the Gallagher Convention Centre in Johannesburg, co-locating five expos: Securex South Africa, A-OSH Expo, Facilities Management Expo, Firexpo, and RE+ South Africa. One free badge grants access to all five shows. The event targets decision-makers dealing with South Africa's energy constraints, compliance pressures, and fragmented operational systems, offering a venue to compare security, safety, facilities, fire protection, and energy solutions side by side and understand how they integrate in practice.

recent_posts.title: Why 2G will outlast 3G in South Africa
recent_posts.summary: Vodacom plans to shut down its 3G network before its 2G network in South Africa, a counterintuitive move driven by persistent demand for ultra-cheap 2G handsets and legacy machine-to-machine devices like wildlife trackers and vehicle sensors. A 4G smartphone still costs over 16% of South Africa's basic minimum wage, making migration difficult. Government has removed luxury duties on low-cost smartphones, and operators like Vodacom and MTN have introduced subsidised 4G devices at R249 and R99 respectively. Most 3G devices can fall back to 2G, making 3G redundant sooner. Operators plan to re-farm legacy spectrum for 4G and 5G as subscriber migration progresses over the next five to ten years.

recent_posts.title: MultiChoice, Altech face prosecution over alleged pay-TV pact
recent_posts.summary: South Africa's Competition Commission has referred MultiChoice and decoder manufacturer Altech UEC to the Competition Tribunal, alleging the two companies entered a market-division agreement in February 2014 in which Altech agreed not to compete with MultiChoice in the pay-TV market. The commission is seeking administrative penalties of up to 10% of each company's annual turnover. The alleged agreement came to light despite Altech launching the Altech Node product seven months later — a device its CEO described as 'not a direct challenge to MultiChoice'. The Node failed commercially and was wound down by late 2015. Altech UEC was subsequently sold to Chinese-owned Skyblu Technologies in 2019. The referral comes 12 years after the alleged collusive conduct, with no explanation given for the delay.

recent_posts.title: CambriLearn on the right way to use AI in schools
recent_posts.summary: CambriLearn, an accredited international online school with 20 years of experience and 80,000+ students across 100+ countries, argues that AI in K-12 education must be deployed as a tool within a qualified-teacher-led structure rather than as a standalone AI tutor. Citing Pew Research data showing 54% of US teens use AI for schoolwork and Brookings findings that current AI deployment risks outweigh benefits, CambriLearn positions its approach — evaluating every AI tool against whether it helps teachers teach better and students learn better — as the sustainable model. The piece contrasts this with failures like Byju's AI-first approach and warns that operators who merely license a model and build a UI on top will not survive the current cycle.

recent_posts.title: TCS | The Cape Town start-up listening for TB with AI
recent_posts.summary: Cape Town-based AI Diagnostics has raised R85-million in a pre-series-A round to deploy the Ostium, an AI-powered digital stethoscope that detects tuberculosis from lung sounds in real time. The device pairs with a proprietary AI.TB model and targets point-of-care use by nurses, pharmacists, and community health workers in resource-constrained settings across Africa and Asia. CEO Braden van Breda discusses how the AI model catches TB signals that trained clinicians miss, the challenge of building a TB-positive lung-sound dataset, handling noisy real-world recording conditions, model drift prevention across geographies, WHO certification goals, and the ambition to place an Ostium in every primary healthcare clinic on the continent by 2030.

recent_posts.title: Colossal Biosciences adds bluebuck antelope to its de-extinction program
recent_posts.summary: Dallas-based Colossal Biosciences has added the bluebuck — a South African antelope hunted to extinction around 1800 — as the sixth species in its de-extinction portfolio. The company is currently in the genome-editing phase, modifying cells of the roan antelope (the bluebuck's closest living relative, sharing over 98% genomic similarity) to introduce bluebuck-specific traits. DNA was sourced from a mounted specimen at the Swedish Museum of Natural History. The next steps involve creating embryos from edited cells and implanting them into surrogate roan mothers, with gestation taking roughly nine months. Colossal CEO Ben Lamm also highlighted that the technology could benefit living threatened antelope species, and defended de-extinction efforts as a necessary complement to conventional conservation, which he argues is failing to keep pace with species loss.

recent_posts.title: US-China tech split deepens
recent_posts.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission has unanimously advanced proposals to bar Chinese labs from testing electronics sold in the US — currently handling about 75% of all US device testing — and to prohibit China Mobile, China Telecom, and China Unicom from operating data centres in the US. The FCC is also considering banning interconnection with carriers using equipment from Huawei and ZTE. These moves extend a series of recent actions including bans on Chinese drones, consumer routers, and equipment imports from companies on the national security 'covered list'.

recent_posts.title: GameStop guns for eBay
recent_posts.summary: GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen has proposed a $56-billion cash-and-stock acquisition of eBay at $125/share, representing a 20% premium. GameStop has already acquired a 5% stake in eBay and secured a $20-billion debt commitment from TD Bank. Cohen argues combining GameStop's 1,600 US retail locations with eBay's platform could create a legitimate Amazon competitor, with $2-billion in annual cost cuts planned within 12 months. The deal would be unusual as GameStop's market cap of ~$12 billion is roughly four times smaller than eBay's ~$46 billion. Cohen has indicated willingness to pursue a proxy fight if eBay's board is unreceptive.
